div.div: the grid version of the same fix

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 758px; height: 1px; padding-top: 461px; margin-left: 38px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: var(--dg-info-fg);

display: inline-block; font-size: 9px; font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans',-apple-system,BlinkMacSystemFont,'Segoe UI',Roboto,sans-serif; color: var(--dg-info-fg); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div: Modern defaults worth adopting now: container queries (a component responds to its own width), logical properties (margin-inline, padding-block — they flip in RTL), and clamp() instead of three breakpoints.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 756px; height: 1px; padding-top: 511px; margin-left: 40px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: var(--dg-warn-fg);

display: inline-block; font-size: 12px; font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans',-apple-system,BlinkMacSystemFont,'Segoe UI',Roboto,sans-serif; color: var(--dg-warn-fg); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div: Nesting is the normal case, not a compromise: a grid page shell whose header is a flex row. Reach for grid when alignment crosses both axes, flex when it does not, and let flow keep doing what it already does well.
